page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This low-memory profile is paired with 3780 GB of local storage and premium storage capabilities, though it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64alds_v7 demonstrates strong compute and memory capabilities. Its single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, single-threaded gzip compression, and PassMark CPU score all rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core stress-ng performance, PassMark CPU physics, and encryption tests fall within the strong top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks consistently register in the top 25%. For database workloads, PassMark database operations rank in the top 10%, complemented by strong top 25% performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

The instance's hardware profile presents distinct architectural tradeoffs. While its high-frequency AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier single-core execution and strong multi-threaded performance, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio limits its suitability for memory-bound applications. Large-scale LLM inference benchmarks reflect this constraint, with prompt processing and text generation for a 70B model dropping to average (middle 50%) performance, whereas smaller 135M and 7B models achieve top-tier to strong execution speeds. Consequently, this server is highly optimized for compute-heavy tasks, local-storage-dependent databases, web serving, and moderate-scale machine learning inference rather than memory-intensive enterprise databases.
description: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 3780 GB of local storage. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and PassMark database operations, alongside strong multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a low-memory tradeoff, making it highly efficient for compute-intensive workloads rather than memory-heavy applications. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in small-model LLM inference and single-threaded compression, but performance drops to average for large 70B LLM models. It supports premium storage and advanced vector extensions but includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This server is best suited for high-throughput web serving, local-storage-dependent databases, and compute-heavy batch processing.
